patients.summary: Graduate student and Army Reservist with primary sclerosing cholangitis on ursodiol who joins in 2019. Extensive ulcerative colitis in 2022 and pemphigus vulgaris in 2023 (prednisone, rituximab), then acute pulmonary histoplasmosis after caving in 2025 and visceral leishmaniasis after a desert deployment later that year. Outside records arrive unevenly.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 24 y/o grad student who moved into the area for his program and wants a primary care doctor he can reach between visits. Says he has a liver condition (PSC) followed by a GI group and takes ursodiol. Membership and insurance info reviewed (university student plan, also has TRICARE Reserve Select through the Army Reserve). New patient visit booked 9/10 at 8:40. Records release sent to his email for the prior GI office and the university health service.

conditions.label: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
conditions.note: Diagnosed at an outside GI group after abnormal liver tests; MRCP-confirmed. Followed by GI/hepatology.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth three times daily

social.value: Rare, 1-2 drinks per month; limits alcohol because of liver disease

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
24M here to establish. Started a doctoral program this fall, also drills one weekend a month with an Army Reserve unit.

PSC: found about a year ago when routine labs showed high liver enzymes; MRCP at the GI group he was seeing confirmed sclerosing cholangitis. Has been on ursodiol 300 mg three times a day since. He sees GI/hepatology yearly with an MRCP, next due in November. No itching, jaundice, RUQ pain or fevers. Bowels normal, no blood. Told he has no colitis that anyone knows of.

Meds: ursodiol 300 mg TID.
Allergies: none to medications.
PMH: as above. PSH: none.
FH: mother has rheumatoid arthritis. A maternal uncle has ulcerative colitis.
SH: single, lives in an apartment with a roommate. Never used tobacco. Drinks maybe once or twice a month at most because of the liver. No drugs. Immunizations largely done through the Army (hep A/B series, Tdap) and college; will send copy.

ROS: negative in detail.

Exam: well-appearing, thin. Vitals as charted. No scleral icterus. Oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly. Skin without jaundice, excoriations or rash. No edema.

A/P:
1. Primary sclerosing cholangitis on ursodiol. Baseline CMP, GGT, CBC today. Will get prior GI notes and MRCP report. Keep yearly hepatology follow-up. Alcohol minimal, fine.
2. Health maintenance: HIV and hep C screening today; HBsAb to document immunity given liver disease. Lipids once. Flu shot when this season's supply comes in. PHQ-2 negative.
Return in a year for a physical, labs every 6 months or so between GI visits.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Rowan, your labs are back. Alkaline phosphatase and GGT are up and ALT sits at the top of normal, which is the usual pattern with PSC and fits what your GI group has been seeing. Bilirubin, albumin, kidney function, blood counts and platelets are all normal. Cholesterol is fine. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative, and your hepatitis B antibody shows you are immune from the Army series. Nothing to change. Bring the November GI letter up with me when it comes.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM to left deltoid. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. VIS reviewed. Tolerated well, left after 15 minutes.

documents.title: Hepatology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology and hepatology group. Date of visit 11/12/2019.

Thank you for following Mr. Sears with us. He is a 24-year-old graduate student with primary sclerosing cholangitis diagnosed last year, here for his yearly review.

He feels well. No pruritus, jaundice, fevers or abdominal pain. Bowel habits are normal without bleeding. Taking ursodiol 300 mg three times daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: anicteric, abdomen soft and nontender, no palpable liver edge or spleen.

MRCP this month: multifocal stricturing and beading of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts, unchanged from last year; no dominant stricture, no mass. Liver and spleen normal in size.
Labs: alkaline phosphatase and GGT elevated in his usual range; bilirubin normal; CA 19-9 within normal limits.

Impression: PSC, stable.
Plan: continue ursodiol at current dose. Repeat MRCP and CA 19-9 in a year. Liver panel every six months with you would be helpful. Should he develop rectal bleeding or a change in bowel habit, please send him back sooner, given the association with colitis.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax for ursodiol 300 mg caps, #270, 90-day. Last LFTs September, GI saw him November. Pended to PCP, approved with 3 refills.

documents.title: Form for my Reserve unit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my unit is doing medical readiness updates remotely since drills are off for now. They want a provider to sign a short form listing my conditions and meds. I uploaded it. No rush, I think the deadline is end of the month.

documents.title: RE: Form for my Reserve unit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Signed and uploaded back to your portal documents. I listed PSC and the ursodiol, nothing else. Stay well.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Masked visit. Year has been strange with classes remote but he's healthy. Teaching a lab section by video. Reserve drills partly virtual.

PSC: GI letter from last November reviewed: MRCP stable, CA 19-9 normal. No itch, jaundice or abdominal pain. Stools normal. Taking ursodiol three times a day, occasionally misses the midday dose.
Meds: ursodiol 300 mg TID. NKDA.
Social: no tobacco, rare drink. Running a few times a week.

Exam: vitals as charted. Anicteric. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Skin clear. Mood good, PHQ-2 is 1.

A/P: healthy 25M with stable PSC. LFTs, CBC, BMP today. Flu vaccine in two weeks when the nurse clinic opens. GI annual visit next month. Physical again in a year.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine given IM, right deltoid. Afebrile, no COVID symptoms on screening. Observed 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: Hepatology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology and hepatology group. Visit 10/20/2020.

Rowan returns for annual PSC review. Asymptomatic. No change in bowel habit. Medication: ursodiol 300 mg TID. NKDA.

Exam benign, anicteric, no hepatosplenomegaly.

MRCP 10/2020: biliary pattern of PSC with multifocal strictures and segmental dilation, stable compared with 2019. No dominant stricture. No mass or new findings.
CA 19-9 normal. Liver enzymes at his baseline per your September labs.

Assessment: stable PSC without progression.
Plan: continue ursodiol; annual MRCP and CA 19-9; six-monthly liver tests in primary care. Will see him in a year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rowan, your liver tests look like your usual PSC numbers, with no rise in bilirubin. Blood counts and platelets normal. Next set in the fall with your physical.

documents.title: COVID shots
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got both Pfizer doses at the campus vaccine clinic (April 13 and May 4). Photo of the card attached so you have it.

documents.title: RE: COVID shots
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks! Both doses entered in your immunization record from the card.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 26M, PSC, yearly exam. Back on campus. Did a two-week annual training with his Reserve unit in July without problems. Feels well. No pruritus, jaundice, fevers, weight change or GI bleeding. Fully vaccinated for COVID in the spring.
Meds: ursodiol 300 mg three times daily. Allergies: NKDA.

O: vitals as charted. Sclerae white. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen nontender, no organomegaly. No rash.

A/P:
- PSC, stable on ursodiol. CMP and CBC today. Hepatology visit next month.
- Prevention: flu shot at nurse clinic in October. PHQ-2 negative. HIV/HCV done 2019.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine IM left deltoid, lot and expiration in the immunization record. No issues during the wait.

documents.title: GI visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Rowan, did your yearly visit with the liver group happen in October? We haven't received a letter yet.

documents.title: RE: GI visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Yes, went on the 19th. MRI was the same as before, they said everything was stable and to keep the ursodiol. I'll ask them to send the note.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Request for the October 2021 hepatology office note and MRCP report faxed to the outside GI group with the patient's signed release on file.
